rationale: Round 1 built and passed, so I am pushing security upward while guarding the hot loop. fasta is dominated by a single arithmetic-heavy main (961 of 999 text bytes) with a tight sequence-generation loop, so SUB gets the highest SecurityGain weight since arithmetic identity substitution adds strong semantic resistance with minimal per-iteration cost. FLA and BCF are weighted high to obscure the loop/control structure of main, but their RuntimeCost weights (0.6) keep the selector from over-applying them inside the hot loop where dispatch and predicate checks would compound. SPLIT is cheap and complements FLA by scattering basic blocks, so it stays enabled with low cost weights. IBR is kept at moderate-high security (0.7) with elevated RuntimeCost/CorrectnessRisk weights to limit its use to non-loop-critical blocks, since indirect branching in the hot loop is the main correctness/perf hazard. ICALL and IGV are retained at lower weights because this program has almost no call sites or globals (only main and _start), so their feature match is weak anyway; the moderate CorrectnessRisk weights prevent forced application where they add risk without payoff. Overall, DiversityGain is kept near SecurityGain for all passes to maximize structural uniqueness against signature matching, while SizeCost stays low-to-moderate given the tiny 1 KB text baseline leaves ample size headroom.
